competitive_landscape: Served by diesel water-taxi lines (Belize Water Taxi / San Pedro Belize Express) from Belize City and San Pedro, plus Tropic Air/Maya Island Air puddle-jumpers. Crossings are frequent but wet, noisy and weather-sensitive; there is no premium or zero-emission option on the reef.

journeys.today: ~45 min on a crowded diesel water taxi, exposed to chop and spray.
journeys.with_navier: A smooth, silent foiling reef transfer — dry, fast and zero-wake over the marine reserve.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Belize City ↔ Caye Caulker ↔ San Pedro reef corridor is squarely in Pioneer II range on sheltered inside-reef water — a premium, zero-wake alternative to the diesel taxis the reef permits gladly.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required on the inside-reef cayes; reserved for any future open-water Belize–atoll legs (Turneffe / Lighthouse).

precedents.why_it_matters: At-scale proof that clean foiling island mobility works on a barrier-reef archipelago — directly transferable to the Belize cayes.

regulatory_note: Operations touch the Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System (a UNESCO World Heritage site) and Hol Chan Marine Reserve — zero-wake, zero-emission foiling is uniquely suited to protected reef waters. Authority engagement via the Belize Port Authority and Fisheries Department.
seasonality: Peak Nov–Apr (dry season); Jun–Nov is wetter with occasional tropical-storm windows. Inside-reef water is sheltered year-round and foiling smooths the typical trade-wind chop.

Caye Caulker ↔ San Pedro / Ambergris Caye

summary: Caye Caulker is a car-free sand caye on the Belize Barrier Reef, a backpacker- and diver-favourite a short hop north of Belize City and just south of Ambergris Caye. Every arrival is by water taxi or small plane; the reef, the Split and the Hol Chan/Shark-Ray Alley dive sites define demand.
tagline: “Go slow” island on the Belize Barrier Reef — reached only by water.

use_cases.body: A premium, silent foiling link from Belize City and San Pedro to a car-free caye — dry and fast where the diesel taxis are wet and loud.
